entries.raw: ::A [[suicide bombing]] attack in [[Kabul]] kills at least two people. [http://uk.reuters.com/article/2014/11/18/uk-afghanistan-blast-idUKKCN0J206920141118 (Reuters)], [http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/stories/A/AS_AFGHANISTAN?SITE=AP&SECTION=HOME&TEMPLATE=DEFAULT&CTIME=2014-11-17-22-45-51 (AP)]
entries.text: A suicide bombing attack in Kabul kills at least two people.,

entries.raw: :[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]:
entries.text: Israeli–Palestinian conflict:

entries.raw: ::Four rabbis (three American and one British) are killed, and eight other people wounded in a [[2014 Jerusalem synagogue massacre|terrorist attack]] on a [[Jerusalem]] [[synagogue]] by two men armed with meat cleavers and guns. The two attackers were killed by police who arrived at the scene. One of the policemen died from his wounds. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-30092720 (BBC)]
entries.text: Four rabbis (three American and one British) are killed, and eight other people wounded in a terrorist attack on a Jerusalem synagogue by two men armed with meat cleavers and guns. The two attackers were killed by police who arrived at the scene. One of the policemen died from his wounds.

entries.raw: ::[[Benjamin Netanyahu]] vows for a heavy response and blames recent incitement by [[Palestinian government|Palestinian]] leaders as [[Fatah]] officially condemns the attack while [[Hamas]] and [[Islamic Jihad Movement in Palestine|Islamic Jihad]] praise it and call for more similar attacks. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/nov/18/deadly-attack-in-jerusalem-synagogue (The Guardian)]
entries.text: Benjamin Netanyahu vows for a heavy response and blames recent incitement by Palestinian leaders as Fatah officially condemns the attack while Hamas and Islamic Jihad praise it and call for more similar attacks.

entries.raw: :[[UNESCO]] declares the [[Rizal Monument]] in [[Manila]], [[Machu Picchu]] of [[Peru]], [[Camino de Santiago]] of Spain, and the [[Dampier Archipelago]] of Australia as [[List of World Heritage Sites in Danger|World Heritage Sites in Danger]]. [http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/story/388642/lifestyle/artandculture/pia-cayetano-rizal-monument-named-one-of-world-s-threatened-heritage-sitesë (GMA News)]
entries.text: UNESCO declares the Rizal Monument in Manila, Machu Picchu of Peru, Camino de Santiago of Spain, and the Dampier Archipelago of Australia as World Heritage Sites in Danger.

entries.raw: :South Korea launches a new National Safety Agency with more than 10,000 staff to replace the [[Korea Coast Guard]], blamed by [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Park Geun-hye]] for a poor response to the [[sinking of MV Sewol|sinking of MV ''Sewol'']]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/11/18/us-southkorea-ferry-idUSKCN0J20B720141118?feedType=RSS&feedName=topNews (Reuters)]
entries.text: South Korea launches a new National Safety Agency with more than 10,000 staff to replace the Korea Coast Guard, blamed by President Park Geun-hye for a poor response to the sinking of MV Sewol.

entries.raw: :[[November 2014 North American cold wave]]
entries.text: November 2014 North American cold wave

entries.raw: ::[[Lake-effect snow]] pummels areas around the Great Lake states, including [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[Michigan]], [[Wisconsin]] and [[Ohio]], stranding hundreds of vehicles and causing [[Erie County, New York]], to declare a state of emergency. [http://www.weather.com/news/commuter-conditions/lake-effect-snow-new-york-michigan-indiana-ohio-wisconsin-pennsylvania-20141118 (The Weather Channel)]
entries.text: Lake-effect snow pummels areas around the Great Lake states, including New York, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin and Ohio, stranding hundreds of vehicles and causing Erie County, New York, to declare a state of emergency.

entries.raw: :[[Human Rights Watch]] claims that police in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]'s capital [[Kinshasa]] [[Kinshasa#Social issues|had killed]] at least 51 people in [[extrajudicial killing]]s in a crackdown on kuluna gangs last November. [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/da84a9c0b2b04f0a9e0c46407880030f/report-51-killed-congo-police-sweep-vs-gangs (AP)]
entries.text: Human Rights Watch claims that police in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's capital Kinshasa had killed at least 51 people in extrajudicial killings in a crackdown on kuluna gangs last November.

entries.raw: :[[Kenneth Mapp]], an independent, is elected [[Governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands]] in the [[United States Virgin Islands gubernatorial election, 2014|gubernatorial runoff election]] over Democrat [[Donna Christensen]]. [http://www.virginislandsnewsonline.com/en/news/kenneth-e-mapp-wins-in-a-landslide-for-usvi-governor- (Virgin Islands News Online)]
entries.text: Kenneth Mapp, an independent, is elected Governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands in the gubernatorial runoff election over Democrat Donna Christensen.

entries.raw: :Japan's Prime Minister [[Shinzō Abe]] calls a snap [[Japanese general election, 2014|election]] for mid-December, two years ahead of schedule. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-30092633 (BBC)]
entries.text: Japan's Prime Minister Shinzō Abe calls a snap election for mid-December, two years ahead of schedule.

entries.raw: :[[Romanian presidential election, 2014|Romanian presidential election]]:
entries.text: Romanian presidential election:

links.raw: [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Romania)|Foreign minister of Romania]]

entries.raw: ::[[Teodor Meleșcanu]] becomes the second [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Romania)|Foreign minister of Romania]] in just eight days to resign because of organizational problems which have left thousands of Romanians abroad unable to vote in the elections. [http://www.balkaneu.com/romanian-formin-resigns-flawed-elections-diaspora/ (Independent Balkan News Agency)]
entries.text: Teodor Meleșcanu becomes the second Foreign minister of Romania in just eight days to resign because of organizational problems which have left thousands of Romanians abroad unable to vote in the elections.

entries.raw: :[[2014 Hong Kong protests|Hong Kong protests]]:
entries.text: Hong Kong protests:

entries.raw: ::Hong Kong authorities start dismantling a protest site in [[Admiralty, Hong Kong|Admiralty]] following a court order. [https://web.archive.org/web/20141121120534/http://www.voanews.com/content/hong-kong-police-expected-clear-protest-areas-this-week/2523679.html (Voice of America)]
entries.text: Hong Kong authorities start dismantling a protest site in Admiralty following a court order.

links.target: New Zealand Labour Party leadership election, 2014

entries.raw: :[[Andrew Little (New Zealand politician)|Andrew Little]] is [[New Zealand Labour Party leadership election, 2014|elected]] to lead the [[New Zealand Labour Party]] following the resignation of [[David Cunliffe]] in September. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2014-11-18/new-zealand-labour-party-elects-new-leader-after-election-defeat.html (''Bloomberg News'')]
entries.text: Andrew Little is elected to lead the New Zealand Labour Party following the resignation of David Cunliffe in September.

entries.raw: :The [[United States Senate]] narrowly defeats legislation on the [[Keystone Pipeline|Keystone XL Pipeline]], intended to allow oil from the [[oil sands]] of Canada to flow to the [[Gulf Coast]] of [[Texas]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2014/11/19/us/politics/keystone-xl-pipeline.html?_r=0 (''New York Times'')]
entries.text: The United States Senate narrowly defeats legislation on the Keystone XL Pipeline, intended to allow oil from the oil sands of Canada to flow to the Gulf Coast of Texas.

entries.text: Jamaica win the 2014 Caribbean Cup defeating Trinidad and Tobago in the final following a penalty shootout.
